title: Keywords and Co-Occurrence Patterns in the Voynich Manuscript: An Information-Theoretic Analysis
authors: Marcelo A. Montemurro and Damián H. Zanette
summary: The authors compare how EVA word tokens are distributed across contiguous blocks with their expected distribution after global token shuffling. They group folios by illustration-defined section and also compare word-frequency profiles across those sections.
established: The word-distribution information statistic peaks at a block size of 807 tokens, close to the peak scales reported for the English, Latin, and Chinese examples. The shuffle baseline preserves each word type's total count.

Among the 100 highest-ranked words, several pairs with similar section-frequency profiles share visible EVA prefixes or suffixes. The link significance calculation shuffles section indices independently for each word's frequency vector.

open.question: Can a fixed table-and-grille or self-citation procedure match the observed word-distribution information curve against global shuffles?
open.check: Freeze the generator and block sizes using public pages, then compare the curve on matched token counts with the published frequency-preserving shuffle statistic.
